claims.statement: URE reported 6,259 refusals of grid-connection conditions for renewable projects in 2024, representing applications totaling just under 42.4 GW; repeated applications mean this capacity is not unique project capacity.

The Polish regulator has identified digitisation, commercial connections, and cable pooling as ways to improve connection transparency or use constrained capacity, and reported early cable-pooling applications and agreements.

Hypothesis: installers and small developers will pay for a pre-application viability screen when its price is materially below engineering rework, delay, or another failed filing; this requires paid-pilot validation.

contrary_evidence: URE cautions that refused-capacity totals include repeat applications, so headline gigawatts overstate unique unmet projects.
Connection decisions remain operator-specific engineering and legal judgments; historical patterns may not predict a particular feeder or future reinforcement.

economics.acquisition_route: Family-company pilots, electrical designers, installer referrals, trade webinars without founder-on-camera dependence, and free local grid-friction reports
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: reach 150 teams at roughly 24,000 PLN annual recurring revenue plus project fees, producing 3.6-5.0m PLN revenue; a profitable data/SaaS business with majority founder ownership could plausibly support over 5m PLN founder equity in four to seven years
economics.founder_time: About 15-20 hours weekly for an eight-week pilot, then 8-12 hours weekly with contracted electrical review and support
economics.gross_margin_basis: Software and analyst-assisted reports should reach 70-85% gross margin after templates and extraction mature; external engineering review is passed through or separately priced
economics.payback: Target customer payback from one avoided unsuitable-site workup or one shorter rework cycle; vendor CAC payback target under six months
economics.pricing: Hypothesis: 900-2,000 PLN per screening, 3,000-8,000 PLN per assisted dossier, or 1,500-4,000 PLN monthly per team
economics.retention_or_repeat: Project-based repeat for active developers; subscriptions retain if outcome data and templates improve across a multi-site pipeline

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A proprietary graph linking sites, feeder evidence, application choices, operator responses, timelines, and outcomes
fingerprint.customer: Polish renewable installers and small solar, storage, or hybrid-project developers
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Pilot through the family installer, then engineering-partner referrals, installer associations, and searchable feeder-level briefings
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Connection-feasibility intelligence plus dossier SaaS, priced per project and by subscription
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Installer or developer pays per screened site, per submitted dossier, or for a recurring team workspace
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A new site needs a grid-connection strategy or an application has been delayed, returned, or refused

founder_fit: Strong fit with data science, AI document extraction, Poland, and a low-social-energy B2B workflow. The family renewable installer can provide a lawful pilot channel and domain feedback without using employer data. The founder should keep engineering sign-off with qualified partners.
risks: A wrong viability estimate could cause costly reliance, requiring careful disclaimers and human engineering review.
DSO process changes could invalidate learned features and templates.
Consultancies or incumbents could bundle equivalent software with connection engineering.

structure.control_point: The pre-application site decision and the evidence-complete connection dossier
structure.critical_dependency: Lawful, sufficiently granular DSO and customer-contributed outcome data

thesis: Build a decision-and-dossier platform for Polish solar, storage, and hybrid-project installers that predicts connection friction, assembles evidence-complete applications, and proposes cable-pooling or commercial-connection alternatives. The defensible asset is a parcel-to-feeder-to-application-outcome graph built from public material and consented customer outcomes, not merely document automation.
title: GridSlot Intelligence for Polish Renewable Connections
uncertainties: Whether DSOs expose enough stable machine-readable data for useful prediction without privileged access.
Whether customers will contribute complete decision letters and outcome data under usable rights.
Which wedge converts best: screening report, dossier workflow, or cable-pooling partner search.
